fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The earth as battery and salt bridge", "body": "LC King described applying galvanic cells and electrolysis to the sun and moon, treating the oceans as an electrolyte, the earth as a salt bridge, the moon as an anode and the sun as a cathode. He argued that the salt bridge acted as a capacitor that kept the whole cell from burning itself out. He also proposed a low pressure, etheric electrolyte above us, and said a vacuum tube with a little salt in it worked like a communication switch. Topher described his own cosmology of an inertial plane through the heart, and LC King called the two views very similar."}, {"title": "Cavitation and dynamic disequilibrium", "body": "Topher Gardner relayed the view of Viktor Schauberger that electricity was a temperature differential rather than a stream of particles. He argued that nature filled any gap or vacuum, and that engineers such as David LaPoint and Tesla built vessels that guided this collapse. Topher said a cavitation pump did not create cavitation but was cavitated by the conditions its builder set up. He also argued that nature lived in dynamic disequilibrium, with both polarities present and one dominant."}, {"title": "Magnets, scalar north and Bedini", "body": "Topher said Floyd Sweet showed that the familiar north and south magnet model was incomplete, and described a ring magnet that drew its field to a central scalar north, which he linked to Polaris. He then recounted the battery reconditioning and side band pulse work of John Bedini, including a school girl wheel that two opposed north poles were said to keep spinning. Topher stressed that he was not an electrical engineer and had only tinkered enough to believe it."}, {"title": "Frequency, mercury and wartime technology", "body": "Topher argued that his Raja yoga training matched what he read of late 1930s German vibrational research, where frequency was location and changing frequency was the way to travel. He described the Nazi bell as spinning mercury with a massive ground current. LC King described a friend using a mercury light bulb to pick up radio stations, and said mercury could grow silver crystals and yield gold under high voltage. He proposed that mercury created the planets. One of the hosts also asked whether imagination itself grew from the sky clock."}, {"title": "The heart, the body and inherited patterns", "body": "Topher cited Dr. Thomas Cowan to argue that the heart was cavitated by the temperature difference between the extremities and the core, described yin and yang polarities from his years as a body worker, and said emotions flowed downstream through families. Chance explained that he sensed distortions in the biofield as ear pressure shifts and read their age and direction, and described how he judged whether a distortion was personal or inherited when a guest asked about miasms. A guest also mentioned muscle testing in kinesiology."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Topher Gardner returns to Vibe Rant to talk about electricity from the fluidic perspective, cavitation technology, dynamic disequilibrium, and other advanced ideas outside of the mainstream materialist comprehension. With LC King bringing his mechanical experience and research to the equation, prepare yourself for an electrifying education!
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "In my opinion, this will be special because it's like the meeting of two minds that really should have met a long time ago. And so here's the intention. Okay. Everybody knows LC King. Everybody knows Topher. But Topher and LC King don't know each other. So this is what we're going to watch happen. Literally, sparks are going to fly.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And what I was doing was applying the galvanic cell and electrolysis to how the sun and moon and all that operate. And so seeing that the oceans are an electrolyte, the earth is a salt bridge and the moon is anode and the sun is a cathode.", "author": "LC King", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/cfdef476-971b-4d87-823e-f9d7d3874b4e/LC+King+InnerVerse+art.PNG?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I just saw it one day. I was like, huh, this is the way structures are supposed to be. Structures are supposed to give the energy that's needed for the structure. It shouldn't be coming from somewhere else. It doesn't need to.", "author": "Topher Gardner", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3d39463d-1ecd-4da7-a921-e0fb460a7301/TOPHER-GARDNER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And this is where you get into sort of plasma stuff as well, where you're able to create plasmas because you basically need three things. You need low pressure, you need heat, and you need a magnetic field.", "author": "LC King", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/cfdef476-971b-4d87-823e-f9d7d3874b4e/LC+King+InnerVerse+art.PNG?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If you don't have the salt bridge there, you take it out, what happens is it goes to equilibrium too fast and just burns itself out. But then when you have the earth or the salt bridge in the way, it acts as a capacitor or a limiter on the whole cell. So it's usually able to generate that electricity over time.", "author": "LC King", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/cfdef476-971b-4d87-823e-f9d7d3874b4e/LC+King+InnerVerse+art.PNG?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Say if you're looking at a vacuum tube, while you're looking at a low pressure system and you're looking at a cathode and anode in that low pressure system with maybe a little bit of salt in there, and there you have a communication device. It's a switch.", "author": "LC King", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/cfdef476-971b-4d87-823e-f9d7d3874b4e/LC+King+InnerVerse+art.PNG?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When you look at an anode and a cathode and you look at the simplest form of a battery basically, which is two electrolytes and a boundary between them. And, you know, this is same as like what your heart is. You've got two different blood types and then you've got a boundary between them. These all just seem like fractals of the same sort of process to me.", "author": "LC King", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/cfdef476-971b-4d87-823e-f9d7d3874b4e/LC+King+InnerVerse+art.PNG?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "So my personal hero, Schauberger, what his hundred questions to science, you know, he was like, well, your model for electricity makes no sense. They just started to pitch the electron model. And he's like, there's no way electricity can be a particle connected to another particle connected to another particle. He goes, electricity is temperature differential.", "author": "Topher Gardner", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3d39463d-1ecd-4da7-a921-e0fb460a7301/TOPHER-GARDNER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's all about how can I engineer the space, the ambiance in a way that allows nature to collapse the field in an additive way, not in a destructive way.", "author": "Topher Gardner", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3d39463d-1ecd-4da7-a921-e0fb460a7301/TOPHER-GARDNER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When you build a cavitation pump, the pump isn't creating the cavitation. It gets cavitated. It's a very odd thing. It's actually your input energy that allows the cavitation to start the pump itself. It's just reacting to the condition that you set in motion.", "author": "Topher Gardner", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3d39463d-1ecd-4da7-a921-e0fb460a7301/TOPHER-GARDNER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's very natural and it creates the dynamic disequilibrium. And that is something I got a lot from Schauberger's work, that in nature you don't have equilibrium. If you have equilibrium, you have death. In a true symbiotic relationship, you have dynamic disequilibrium.", "author": "Topher Gardner", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3d39463d-1ecd-4da7-a921-e0fb460a7301/TOPHER-GARDNER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But eventually I got to the point where I was able to make sort of the agreement with my body that every time I would tell it what I'm looking for, and then when I found what I was looking for, my body would tell me with pressure differential, pressure shift in my eardrums that would cause my ears to pop.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Basically, body knows everything. And it's a matter of getting a language that you can talk to the body through. Kinesiology is a good language.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
